CLINICAL DISCHARGE SUMMARY
PATIENT DEMOGRAPHICS
Patient Name: John Doe
Date of Birth: 05/14/1974
Gender: Male
MRN: 948-204-11A
Date of Admission: 08/01/2180
Date of Discharge: 08/03/2180

CHIEF COMPLAINT
The patient presented with acute chest pain substernal pressure radiating to the left arm, rated 8/10.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Doe is a 52-year-old male with a history of hypertension. ECG showed sinus rhythm with non-specific ST changes. Initial troponin level was elevated at 0.08 ng/mL. He was diagnosed with NSTEMI.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Essential Hypertension.
2. Hyperlipidemia.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals: BP 138/82 mmHg, HR 78 bpm. Lungs clear.

DIAGNOSTICS & LAB RESULTS
Cardiac Troponin I: Initial 0.08, 3h repeat 0.24, 6h repeat 0.42 ng/mL.
Echocardiogram: LVEF of 50% with mild hypokinesis.

ASSESSMENT & PLAN
1. Acute NSTEMI. Patient underwent coronary angiography revealing 75% stenosis in mid-LAD. A drug-eluting stent was deployed successfully.
2. Hypertension: Stable, continue Lisinopril 20 mg.
3. Hyperlipidemia: Start Atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
4. DAPT: Start Clopidogrel 75 mg and Aspirin 81 mg daily.

CLINICAL DISCHARGE SUMMARY
PATIENT DEMOGRAPHICS
Patient Name: Sarah Jenkins
Date of Birth: 03/22/1988
Gender: Female
MRN: 312-984-75B
Date of Admission: 11/10/2185
Date of Discharge: 11/12/2185

CHIEF COMPLAINT
Fatigue, severe nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Ms. Jenkins is a 37-year-old female with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus who presented with a 2-day history of progressive lethargy, nausea, vomiting, and diffuse abdominal discomfort. She reports missing multiple insulin doses due to a stomach flu. On arrival, she was tachypneic with Kussmaul respirations and fruity odor on breath.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus - diagnosed age 12.
2. Diabetic retinopathy.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals: BP 102/60 mmHg, HR 112 bpm (tachycardia), RR 24 bpm, Temp 36.8 C, O2 Sat 99% on room air.
General: Dry mucous membranes, skin turgor reduced (moderate dehydration).

DIAGNOSTICS & LAB RESULTS
- Blood Glucose: 450 mg/dL (hyperglycemia).
- Arterial Blood Gas (ABG): pH 7.15, HCO3 12 mEq/L (severe metabolic acidosis).
- Serum Ketones: Strongly positive (3+).
- Urinalysis: Glucose 4+, Ketones 4+.
- BMP: Sodium 132 mEq/L (mild hyponatremia), Potassium 5.2 mEq/L.

ASSESSMENT & PLAN
1. Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA): Triggered by insulin non-compliance. Corrected with aggressive IV fluid resuscitation (normal saline) and continuous intravenous insulin infusion. Potassium was replaced. Transitioned to subcutaneous basal-bolus insulin once anion gap closed and eating tolerated.
2. Dehydration: Resolved with IV fluids.
3. Diabetes Education: Re-educated on sick-day rules and insulin administration.
